The Siemens MS43 engine control unit (ECU) uses an Infineon C167CR_SR CPU clocked at 24MHz in combination with a 4 megabit AMD AM29F400BB flash memory.

This ECU controls the BMW M54 inline six engine.

When looking at the cryptic item names this might help you: [[Siemens Keyword Translation]]
<div style="float:right;">__TOC__</div>

'''Bootloader Section'''

This section is 64 kilobytes in size and contains the boot code that initializes the ecu and verifies that everything is ok before control is handed over to the program code section. This section also contains one time writeable data such as immobilizer information and user information fields (UIF).

'''Program Code Section'''

This section is 384 kilobytes in size and contains the program code that operates the engine.

'''Calibration Data Section'''

This section is 64 kilobytes in size and contains the calibration data that the program code uses to operate the engine.

=Checksums=
The MS43 uses three CRC16 checksums that verifies the data integrity of the boot, program and calibration sections and two 32-bit addition checksums that verifies the data integrity of the system monitoring (_mon) parameters. 
If any of the checksums are incorrect the ecu assumes that the data on flash has been corrupted and it won't allow the engine to start.

When correcting all the checksums the addition checksums has to be corrected '''before''' the CRC16 checksums, as the addition checksums are located inside the CRC16 checksum areas.

The checksums are located at the following addresses:

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:left;"
!CRC16
!Location
|-
| Boot
| 0x3C24
|-
| Program
| 0x6FDE0
|-
| Calibration
| 0x73FE0
|-
!32-bit Addition
!Location
|-
| Program
| 0x6FDAE
|-
| Calibration
| 0x72FFC
|-
|}

==Disabling Calibration Checksums==
'''Warning:''' It's not advised to disable the calibration checksums as the ECU looses the ability to verify the data integrity of the calibration data. This section is provided solely for educational purposes to explain how the factory bypass is performed.

'''Disable CRC16 Checksum'''

To disable the CRC16 calibration checksum do the following.

; Hexeditor
: 1. Set Word at 0x73FFE to 0xFFFF
: 2. Set Byte at 0x6FFB0 to 0xA8
: 3. Change the Byte in the table from 0x84 to 0x94

=Variants Configuration=
As the MS43 ecu is used in many different chassis configurations it uses a combination of configuration switches and automatic learning routines to detect which features or behaviors should be enabled.

==Switches==

'''Configuration switch - Anti jerk load signal reference variant (c_conf_aj_maf)'''
*0: MAF signal referenced
*1: MAF substitute referenced

'''Configuration switch - Brake light test switch logic variant (c_conf_bts)'''
*0: Signal high corresponds to 'brake pedal pressed'
*1: Signal low corresponds to 'brake pedal pressed'

'''Configuration switch - CAN-bus calibration logic variant (c_conf_can_cal)'''
*0: CAN-bus calibration logic not active
*1: CAN-bus calibration logic active

'''Configuration switch - Lambda sensor configuration (c_conf_cat)'''
*0: Automatic variant learning — Single bank system with one control (pre-cat) sensor, or CATV variant (SA199)
*1: Automatic variant learning — Dual bank system with two control (pre-cat) sensors, or CATV variant (SA199)
*2: Single bank system — 1 control (pre-cat) sensor and 1 monitoring (post-cat) sensor
*3: Dual bank system — 2 control (pre-cat) sensors and 2 monitoring (post-cat) sensors
*4: Automatic variant learning — Dual bank system, with or without control (pre-cat) and monitoring (post-cat) sensors, or CATV variant (SA199)

;Procedure After Changing c_conf_cat
:# Disconnect all lambda sensors that are not required for the selected configuration.
:# Reset the “learned variants” adaptation in the ECU. This step ensures the ECU re-learns the correct lambda sensor configuration during the next startup.

'''Configuration switch - Alternator charge balancing (c_conf_cha_cdn_bat)'''
*0: Charge balancing not active
*1: Charge balancing active for manual transmission
*2: Charge balancing active for automatic transmission
*3: Charge balancing active for manual and automatic transmission

'''Configuration switch - Main switch cruise control (c_conf_cru_main_swi)'''
*0: Main switch function active, main switch controlled over steering wheel button O/I
*1: Main switch function inactive for Z3 usage, main switch enabled when ignition key voltage is present

'''Configuration switch - DMTL module (c_conf_dmtl)'''
*0: DMTL module not present, function and diagnosis not active
*1: DMTL module present, function and diagnosis active

'''Configuration switch - Electrical cooling fan (c_conf_ecf)'''
*0: Electrical cooling fan not present, function and diagnosis not active
*1: Electrical cooling fan present, function and diagnosis active

'''Configuration switch - Exhaust flap (c_conf_ef)'''
*0: Exhaust flap not present, function and diagnosis not active
*1: Exhaust flap present, function and diagnosis active

'''Configuration switch - EOBD (c_conf_eobd)'''
*0: Distance travelled with MIL On reporting via OBD not active
*1: Distance travelled with MIL On reporting via OBD active

'''Configuration switch - Lambda sensor diagnosis of secondary air valve (c_conf_lam_sav_diag)'''
*0: Lambda diagnostic of secondary air valve not active
*1: Lambda diagnostic of secondary air valve active

'''Configuration switch - Malfunction indicator light variant with monitoring lambda sensors (c_conf_mil)'''
*0: Malfunction indicator light not active
*1: Malfunction indicator light active when BMW specific faults are set
*2: Malfunction indicator light active when OBDII faults or component errors are set after 2nd driving cycle
*3: Malfunction indicator light active when OBDII faults or component errors are set immediately

'''Configuration switch - Malfunction indicator light variant without monitoring lambda sensors (c_conf_mil_eu2)'''
*0: Malfunction indicator light not active
*1: Malfunction indicator light active when BMW defined faults are set
*2: Malfunction indicator light active when OBDII faults or component errors are set after 2nd driving cycle
*3: Malfunction indicator light active when OBDII faults or component errors are set immediately

'''Configuration switch - Engine speed hysteresis handling for fuel cut off. Manual transmission (c_conf_n_hys_puc)'''
*0: Conservative engine speed hysteresis handling active
*1: Responsive engine speed hysteresis handling active

'''Configuration switch - Engine speed hysteresis handling for fuel cut off. Automatic transmission (c_conf_n_hys_puc_dri)'''
*0: Conservative engine speed hysteresis handling active
*1: Responsive engine speed hysteresis handling active

'''Configuration switch - Secondary air pump (c_conf_sap)'''
*0: Automatic learning of secondary air pump configuration
*1: Secondary air pump not present
*2: Secondary air pump present without secondary air flow meter
*3: Secondary air pump present with secondary air flow meter

To re-do the secondary air pump learning process the "learned variants" adaptation needs to cleared in the ecu.

'''Configuration switch - Secondary air valve diagnosis (c_conf_sav_diag)'''
*0: Secondary air valve diagnosis not active
*1: Secondary air valve diagnosis active

'''Configuration switch - Mechanical diagnosis of electrical thermostat based on radiator outlet temperature (c_conf_tco_ex)'''
*0: Mechanical diagnosis of electrical thermostat not active
*1: Mechanical diagnosis of electrical thermostat active

'''Configuration switch - Exhaust gas temperature sensors (c_conf_teg)'''
*0: Automatic learning of exhaust gas temperature sensors
*1: Exhaust gas temperature sensors not present
*2: Three exhaust gas temperature sensors present

To re-do the exhaust gas temperature learning process the "learned variants" adaptation needs to cleared in the ecu.

'''Configuration switch - Pre injection during crank synchronization (c_conf_tipr_end)'''
*0: Allow pre injection during crank synchronization
*1: Abort pre injection during crank synchronization

'''Configuration switch - Torque limitation in first gear (c_conf_tq_lim_gear)'''
*0: First gear torque limiter not active
*1: First gear torque limiter active (E53)

'''Configuration switch - DS2 adaptation write access (c_conf_ad_ena)'''
*0: DS2 adaptation write access not active
*1: DS2 adaptation write access active

== Gearbox Variant Detection ==
To support different gearbox configurations, the ECU monitors the CAN bus for specific CAN messages.
* If the '''EGS1''' CAN message is detected, the gearbox variant is set to Automatic (AT)
* If the '''SSG1''' CAN message is detected, the gearbox variant is set to Automated Manual (AMT)
* If neither message is detected, the gearbox variant defaults to Manual (MT)

Once the detection process is complete, the identified gearbox variant is stored in the on-board EEPROM.

To repeat the gearbox variant learning process, clear the "Learned Variants" adaptation in the ECU.

== Air Conditioning System Detection ==
The ECU determines whether an air conditioning (A/C) system is installed by monitoring the CAN bus for the '''INSTR3''' message.
If this message is detected, the A/C system logic is activated.

Once detection is complete, the result is stored in the on-board EEPROM.
To repeat the A/C system detection process, the “Learned Variants” adaptation must be cleared in the ECU.

== Steering Angle Sensor Detection ==
The ECU automatically detects whether a steering angle sensor is installed by monitoring the CAN bus for the '''LWS1''' message.
If this message is present, the ECU activates the steering angle sensor logic.

Once detection is complete, the result is saved to the on-board EEPROM.

To repeat the steering angle sensor learning process, the "learned variants" adaptation must be cleared in the ECU.

== Ignition Coil Detection ==
During the mid-production phase of the MS43, the original 300g ignition coils were replaced with pencil ignition coils.
To support both ignition coil configurations, hardware revision Index 04 was introduced along with updated detection logic.

The ECU determines the coil type by checking if pin X60002.12 is connected to terminal 87 (main relay output):

* Not connected: 300g ignition coils are installed
* Connected: Pencil ignition coils are installed

Once detection is complete, the result is stored in the on-board EEPROM.

To repeat the ignition coil learning process, the "learned variants" adaptation must be cleared in the ECU.

'''Note:''' If pencil coils are used with an older Index 03 MS43, or with an Index 04 or newer MS43 that does not have the X60002.12 jumper wire retrofitted, the values from the ''_pc'' ignition coil tables can be copied to the corresponding ''_300'' tables.
[[File:Siemens MS43 Coil Data.png|none|none|none|Pencil Coil Data]]

== Ambient Pressure Sensor Detection ==
During the mid-production phase of the MS43, the Motorola ambient pressure sensor was replaced with a smaller Infineon version.
To support both sensor configurations, a new detection logic was introduced.

The ECU determines which sensor type is installed by measuring the voltage on one of the ambient pressure sensor input pins:

* Voltage < c_v_var_amp: Motorola sensor detected

* Voltage ≥ c_v_var_amp: Infineon sensor detected

Once detection is complete, the following values are stored in the ECU’s boot sector at memory address 0x3EEC–0x3EF1:

* Motorola sensor: 0xA5A5A5A5A5A5

* Infineon sensor: 0x5A5A5A5A5A5A 

Because this detection result is stored in the boot sector, the ambient pressure sensor learning process can normally only be performed once during the ECU’s lifetime.
However the learning process can be reset by overwriting the memory area 0x3EEC–0x3EF1 with the value 0xFF with a boot mode write.

=Mass Air Flow Sensor=
[[File:M54B30 MAF Scalar TunerPro.png|thumb|M54B30 MAF Scalar]]
The mass airflow sensor is one of the most important sensors as it allows the engine management system to measure how much air is entering the intake system and it's a key component for many calculations.

MS43 uses a MAF sensor that outputs a 0-5V signal that is then converted to a kg/h reading.

There is also provision for a secondary MAF sensor that was planned to be used to meter the air entering the secondary air pump system but is was never used in production.

The analog signals are converted to a MAF reading in kg/h by the following scalars.
* '''id_maf_tab''' - MAF Sensor Scalar 1x256
* '''id_saf_tab''' - Secondary Air MAF Sensor Scalar 1x256
* '''id_maf_tab__v_maf_1__v_maf_2''' - MAF Sensor Scalar 16x16
* '''id_saf_tab__v_saf_1__v_saf_2''' - Secondary Air MAF Sensor Scalar 16x16

An important note for the sensor definition tables is that there is no configurable voltage scale as the voltage scale is based upon the resolution of the ADC input and no interpolation is performed on the data in the tables.

For better visualization the voltage scale is only included in the 1x256 tables, the 16x16 tables are only numbered.

===Input Monitoring===

To diagnose the mass airflow sensor values the mass airflow sensor input is continuously monitors that the voltage is between the thresholds that are set by the following variables:
*'''c_maf_max_diag''' - Maximum load threshold to trigger a short to positive fault
*'''c_maf_min_diag''' - Minimum load threshold to trigger a short to ground fault

If the voltage falls outside these thresholds an error code will be set for the MAF sensor input and MAF failsafe mode will be activated.

When increasing the engine breathing capabilities '''c_maf_max_diag''' should be raised to a value just above the maximum load values that the engine can produce.

===Failsafe Mode===

In case of a mass airflow sensor failure or malfunction the MAF failsafe mode is activated and the MAF sensor load reading will be substituted with the values from the MAF diagnosis table.

* '''ip_maf_1_diag__n__tps_av''' - MAF diagnosis table used as a load substitute if there is a MAF sensor error
**'''X axis''': throttle position sensor value (tps_av)
**'''Y axis''': engine speed (n)

The MAF diagnosis table is also used during normal operation to filter VANOS load and diagnosis purposes so if the engine is modified to consume more air it's advisable to re-tune the MAF sensor substitute table to keep the load values as accurate as possible.

When doing this it's good practice to data log MAF sensor load, accelerator pedal value and engine speed to create a histogram table that can be used as a base when modifying the MAF sensor substitute table.

'''Note:''' Be aware that the MAF sensor substitute table can not accurately model all factors that affects the engines breathing capabilities so it's not advisable to use it as a replacement for a real MAF sensor.

=Engine Load=
During operation several filtered engine load parameters are created with the most important ones for tuning being the following:
* Injection load (maf_ti)
* Ignition Load (maf_iga)
* VANOS load (maf_ivvt)

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:100%;"
|+ '''Load Derivation Paths'''
|-
! MAF
! MAF failover (Alpha-N)
|-
| Measure air mass via MAF sensor
| Estimate air mass based on ip_maf_1_diag table
|-
| ↓
| ↓
|-
| Estimate manifold pressure based on intake models and measured air mass
| Estimate manifold pressure based on intake models and estimated air mass
|-
| ↓
| ↓
|-
| Calculate load based on estimated manifold pressure and VO tables
| Calculate load based on estimated manifold pressure and VO tables
|}

'''Note:''' Many logging options only reports the engine load measured by the mass airflow sensor that can vary greatly from the filtered loads which can give an incorrect view on what is actually happening.

In boosted applications it's really important that the injection load is monitored and tuned correctly as otherwise the engine will run into a "lean-wall" when hitting positive manifold pressure.
See [[#Extending_VO_Tables_For_Forced_Induction|Extending VO Tables For Forced Induction]] for tuning guidelines.

==Injection Load==
[[File:Siemens MS43 Intake Model.png|thumb|right|Intake Manifold Volume Model]]
The load filtering process for the injection load is used to account for changes in the engines volumetric efficiency due to the variable valve overlap induced by the variable valve timing. This filtration process is in short an optimized version of the speed density control strategy where several steps are pre-calculated and stored in tables which are retrieved at runtime.

'''Calculated Manifold Pressure'''

First the ecu calculates the manifold absolute pressure with the help of Clapeyrons ideal gas equation by taking the effective intake manifold volume, the engine speed, the current airflow reading from the mass airflow sensor and the volumetric efficiency of the engine defined by the vo tables into account.

So for example if the mass airflow sensor measured that 200 mg/stk of air entered the intake manifold and the vo tables defined that the engine at the current intake pressure and engine speed can only consume 100 mg/stk of air then the remaining 100 mg/stk of air must still be inside the intake manifold which increases the pressure inside the intake manifold.

The effective intake volume is different between increasing and decreasing load scenarios and is therefore split up into four different tables:

* '''ip_vol_im__n__maf_mes''' - Effective intake manifold volume at increasing load during part load and full load
* '''ip_vol_im_neg__n__maf_mes''' - Effective intake manifold volume at decreasing load during part load and full load
* '''ip_vol_im_is__n__maf_mes''' - Effective intake manifold volume at increasing load during idle, trailing throttle and trailing throttle fuel cut-off
* '''ip_vol_im_neg_is__n__maf_mes''' - Effective intake manifold volume at decreasing load during idle, trailing throttle and trailing throttle fuel cut-off

The more accurate these models and the MAF sensor readings is, the more accurate the calculated manifold absolute pressure value will be that's used in the next step.

'''Volumetric Efficiency Calculation'''

After the current manifold pressure is calculated 8 volumetric efficiency lookup tables '''ip_maf_vo_[1-8]__map__n''' and a selection table '''ip_nr_ip_maf__vo''' selects the active vo table based on the current valve overlap.

The vo tables can be viewed as speed density lookup tables that contains the pre-calculated results of the speed density formula at different engine speed and intake pressures. The values represent how much air is able to enter the cylinders for a given valve overlap during an engine revolution.

* '''ip_nr_ip_maf__vo''' - Active vo table for speed density calculation
* '''ip_maf_vo_1__map__n''' - Engine volumetric effiency - Valve overlap step 1
* '''ip_maf_vo_2__map__n''' - Engine volumetric effiency - Valve overlap step 2
* '''ip_maf_vo_3__map__n''' - Engine volumetric effiency - Valve overlap step 3
* '''ip_maf_vo_4__map__n''' - Engine volumetric effiency - Valve overlap step 4
* '''ip_maf_vo_5__map__n''' - Engine volumetric effiency - Valve overlap step 5
* '''ip_maf_vo_6__map__n''' - Engine volumetric effiency - Valve overlap step 6
* '''ip_maf_vo_7__map__n''' - Engine volumetric effiency - Valve overlap step 7
* '''ip_maf_vo_8__map__n''' - Engine volumetric effiency - Valve overlap step 8

As the current valve overlap will not always be exactly at the 8 different valve overlap breakpoints defined in the '''ip_nr_ip_maf''' table the ecu will interpolate the load value between the '''ip_maf_vo_[1-8]''' tables so for example if the current valve overlap is halfway between the '''ip_maf_vo_1''' table and the '''ip_maf_vo_2''' table then the ecu will combine half of the load value from the '''ip_maf_vo_1''' table with half of the load value from the '''ip_maf_vo_2''' table.

'''Note:''' In stock form these tables are setup to support manifold pressures between 50hPa and 1250hPa which gives some headroom to compensate for outside ambient pressure. In boosted applications the manifold pressure axis of these tables will need to be extended to allow higher pressures to be processed correctly.  
For boosted applications see [[#Extending_VO_Tables_For_Forced_Induction|Extending VO Tables For Forced Induction]] for tuning guidelines.

'''Coolant temperature correction'''

Due to the speed density calculation being pre-calculated with an assumed temperature of the air entering the cylinders the output from the '''ip_maf_vo_[1-8]__map__n''' tables is multiplied with a correction factor from the '''ip_maf_tco_cor__tco''' table to correct the output for the cooling/heating effect the engine temperature will have on the air entering the cylinders.

==Ignition Load==
To improve the response time for ignition load adjustments the ECU alternates the ignition load (maf_iga) between two load sources:
* Injection Load (maf_ti)
* Filtered MAF Sensor Load (maf_ign)

;Load Filtering Process
:During each load acquisition cycle the ECU will update the maf_ign load with the help of the following calculation:
:maf_ign = maf_ign + (maf_mes - maf_ign) * ip_maf_ign_crlc__n__maf_mes
* '''ip_maf_ign_crlc__n__maf_mes''' - MAF signal filtering constant for maf_ign
;Load Source Selection
:If maf_ign is greater than maf_ti + c_maf_iga_hys then maf_ign will take over as maf_iga.
:And when maf_ign becomes less than maf_ti + c_maf_iga_pas then the ecu will revert back to maf_ti as the source for maf_iga.
* '''c_maf_iga_hys''' - maf_ign activation hysteresis
* '''c_maf_iga_pas''' - maf_ign pacification hysteresis
==VANOS Load==
To create a feedback free VANOS load signal the ECU blend between the MAF sensor load (maf_mes) and the load values from the MAF sensor substitute table (maf_sub_ivvt).

;Load Filtering Process
:During each load acquisition cycle the ECU will update the maf_ivvt load with the help of the following calculations:
:maf_sub_ivvt = (maf_mes - maf_sub_diag) * ip_fac_maf_sub_ivvt__maf_sub_diag + maf_sub_diag
:maf_ivvt = maf_ivvt + (maf_sub_ivvt - maf_ivvt) * ip_crlc_maf_ivvt__n__maf_sub_diag
* '''ip_fac_maf_sub_ivvt__maf_sub_diag''' - maf_sub_ivvt blending factor
* '''ip_crlc_maf_ivvt__n__maf_sub_diag''' - maf_ivvt filtering constant
[[File:Vanos Load Weighting Factor.png]]

;Load Source Selection
:The ip_fac_maf_sub_ivvt blending factor table is setup to mostly rely on the load measured by the MAF sensor during low load and as the load readings start to climb the factor start to gravitate more and more against the readings from the MAF sensor substitute table.

When the engine is modified to consume more air it's advisable to re-tune the MAF sensor substitute table to keep the VANOS load as accurate as possible.
See [[#Failsafe_Mode|MAF Failsafe Mode]] for tuning guidelines.

==Extending VO Tables For Forced Induction==
In stock form the VO tables are setup to support manifold pressures between 50hPa and 1250hPa which gives some headroom to compensate for varying atmospheric pressure. But a boosted applications can easily exceed 1250hPa of pressure so for the ecu to be able to correctly operate above this pressure we need to re-scale the pressure axis for the VO tables.

As the volumetric efficiency scales pretty linearly with the increasing intake pressure above atmospheric pressure (~1000hPa) it's possible to create rough forced induction VO starter tables by extrapolating the data from the last two pressure rows to the desired boost target that the engine will reach plus a couple of extra hPa to give some headroom to accommodate for boost spikes and varying atmospheric pressure.
To help with this we have prepared an Excel sheet that can be used to extrapolate your own tables: 
[[File:Load Filtration Table Extrapolation.zip|thumb|Load_Filtration_Table_Extrapolation.zip]]

On an engine running stock cams the extrapolated VO tables could look something like this if the engine is expected to run a boost target at around 1500hPa with a headroom of 500hPa to accommodate for boost spikes and varying atmospheric pressure.
[[File:Siemens MS43 Load Filtration Boosted.png|800px]]

Please note that this is only an example that should get you in the ballpark so further tuning will be needed for your specific engine configuration, ideally a real map sensor should be connected to the engine to verify that the calculated manifold pressure values are not drifting away due to incorrectly calibrated intake model or VO tables.

After hundreds of kilometers of logging data, we never experienced a measured pressure of under ~150hPa so it can be considered safe to shift the tables and axis values up to clear the last row to be used for the expected maximal pressure that the engine will see.

When doing a M50 manifold conversions it could be a good idea to take a look at the intake models in the Alpina B3S binary, the Alpina manifold is pretty similar to the M50 so the intake model values should be closer than the M54 intake models.

= Injection =

The MS43 ECU calculates fuel injection time from engine load and engine speed. The base injection maps contain injector opening time in milliseconds, which is then corrected by various enrichment, enleanment, compensation, and adaptation strategies to determine the final injector pulse width.

During closed-loop operation, the ECU uses narrowband lambda sensors to maintain a stoichiometric air-fuel ratio. Fuel trim adaptations learned during closed-loop operation are also applied during open-loop operation, including full load.

Although many correction factors contribute to the final injection time, the following calibration tables define the primary fueling strategy.

== Engine Start ==

Before normal engine operation begins, the ECU uses dedicated fuel maps for engine start.

* '''ip_tipr_cst__tco''' – Base pre injection time.
* '''ip_ti_cst__n__tco''' – Base cranking injection time.

== Base Injection Maps ==

During normal operation, the ECU interpolates between separate cold and warm injection maps to account for the cold to warm operation transition of the VANOS system. Individual part-load maps are provided for each cylinder bank.

'''Cold Engine'''

* '''ip_ti_tco_1_is_ivvt__n__maf''' – Base injection time during idle.
* '''ip_ti_tco_1_pl_ivvt_1__n__maf''' – Base injection time for Bank 1 during part load.
* '''ip_ti_tco_1_pl_ivvt_2__n__maf''' – Base injection time for Bank 2 during part load.

'''Warm Engine'''

* '''ip_ti_tco_2_is_ivvt__n__maf''' – Base injection time during idle.
* '''ip_ti_tco_2_pl_ivvt_1__n__maf''' – Base injection time for Bank 1 during part load.
* '''ip_ti_tco_2_pl_ivvt_2__n__maf''' – Base injection time for Bank 2 during part load.

'''Map Axes'''

* '''X-axis''' – Filtered engine load used by the injection subsystem (''maf_ti'')
* '''Y-axis''' – Engine speed (''n'')

The transition between the cold and warm engine state is explained in the VANOS [[Siemens_MS43#Cold-to-Warm_Transition|Cold-to-Warm Transition]] section.

'''VANOS Failsafe Operation'''

If the ECU detects an active VANOS fault, it can no longer accurately predict the cylinder filling produced by the variable camshaft positions.

In this operating mode, the ECU falls back to the fixed base injection table:

* '''ip_tib__n__maf''' – Base injection time used when VANOS control is unavailable.

'''Important:''' After recalibrating the part-load injection maps, this fallback table should also be updated. Otherwise, the engine may run with incorrect fueling whenever the ECU enters VANOS failsafe mode.

== Temperature Correction ==

To compensate for lean air-fuel mixtures during low ambient temperatures and steady state operation the ECU applies the following temperature correction factor to the base injection timing.

* '''ip_ti_fac_n_maf__n__maf''' – Base temperature correction factor.
* '''ip_ti_fac_tia_toil__tia__toil''' – Temperature correction weighting factor - Intake temperature vs oil temperature.
* '''ip_ti_fac_tco__tco''' – Temperature correction weighting factor - Coolant temperature.

== Engine Warm Up ==

To account for the extra fuel that the engine needs during warm-up from a cold start the ECU applies the following warm-up correction factor to the base injection timing.

* '''ip_ti_wup__n__maf''' – Base warm-up correction factor.
* '''ip_ti_tco_wup_is__tco__tco_st''' – Warm-up weighting factor during idle - Coolant temperature vs Coolant temperature at start.
* '''ip_ti_tco_wup__tco__tco_st''' – Warm-up weighting factor - Coolant temperature vs Coolant temperature at start.
* '''ip_ti_vo_wup__tco__vo''' – Warm-up weighting factor - Coolant temperature vs Valve Overlap.

== Full Load Enrichment ==

During full-load operation, the ECU multiplies the calculated part-load injection time by an enrichment factor from the following table:

* '''ip_ti_fl__n''' – Full-load enrichment factor

The purpose of this enrichment is to reduce combustion temperatures, protect the engine from knock, and increase exhaust component durability under high load.

'''Viewing the Table as Lambda or AFR'''

[[File:Full_Load_Injection_AFR_Lambda.png|thumb|right|Full load injection converted to Lambda and AFR]]

For easier calibration, the conversion factor of '''ip_ti_fl__n''' can be modified so that the table displays either Lambda or Air-Fuel Ratio (AFR) instead of the internal enrichment factor.

'''Important:''' The displayed Lambda or AFR values are only achieved if the base injection maps are correctly calibrated to produce stoichiometric combustion (Lambda = 1.00) before full-load enrichment is applied.

{| class="wikitable"
! Table Display
! Conversion Formula
! Minimum
! Maximum
|-
| Lambda
| 1-(0.0039058823 × X - 0.5)
| 0.500
| 1.500
|-
| AFR (Gasoline)
| 14.7-(14.7 × (0.0039058823 × X - 0.5))
